listing.description:
Sol System is the strategic simulation and canonical-world layer behind the wider Sol universe. It runs the coarse strategic game: factions, fleets, orbital infrastructure, construction projects, resource logistics, missions, invasions, salvage, system events and the long-running state that connects one session to the next.

The simulation operates across a 3D system surface with persistent stars, planets, moons, stations, strategic ships and structures. Fleets retain roles, allegiance, orders and strategic tasks such as patrol, escort, mining, hauling, scouting, guarding and interception. Sol Command provides the persistent home-system faction, orbital presence and a growing strategic force rather than treating the universe as a collection of isolated encounters.

Construction is part of the canonical simulation. Stations, shipyards, sensor arrays, mining rigs and military craft consume treasury and strategic time, with project progress, cancellation and completion written by the Sol System authority. Resource chains and faction stockpiles feed the same strategic layer.

Strategic time is deliberately separate from cockpit animation. Ordinary local flight, warp and multiple connected pilots can request different relativity bubbles, while Sol System preserves a single shared strategic clock and prevents one client from independently fast-forwarding the world. Planetary ephemerides, fleet positions and project progress remain authoritative at the strategy layer while local movement stays fluid in Explorer.

Universe Admin exposes fine-grained control over factions, ships, weapons, stations, missions, events and canonical scheduling for development and live-world operation. The canonical bridge persists world snapshots and an append-only journal, publishes compact system scenes, handles player presence and distributes strategic updates to connected Explorer clients.

The public Showcase build demonstrates the browser-local strategic simulation without the private canonical bridge service. Shared persistence, multiplayer authority and canonical admin mutations therefore remain unavailable in the demo, while the core strategy and simulation surface can still be explored locally.

world snapshots and durable system state
